title: Grammar: Hedging Language in Academic and Scientific Writing
grammarTip:
Хеджирование (Hedging) — смягчение утверждений в академическом письме:

Хеджирующие глаголы:
seem · appear · suggest · indicate · tend to · be likely to
"The results suggest that..." · "The data appear to indicate..."

Модальные глаголы для хеджирования:
may · might · could · should · would
"This could explain why..." · "There may be a connection..."

Наречия-хеджеры:
apparently · seemingly · presumably · generally · typically
"This is generally considered to be..." · "It is typically assumed..."

Структуры:
"It seems / appears that..." · "It is possible that..."
"It is widely believed that..." · "There is evidence to suggest..."

💡 В академическом письме хеджирование = интеллектуальная честность, а не слабость!

grammarTable.subject: Modal verbs
grammarTable.example: "The effect may be larger in older populations." / "This could suggest a different mechanism."

grammarTable.subject: Hedging verbs
grammarTable.verb: suggest / indicate / appear / seem / tend to
grammarTable.example: "The data suggests a correlation." / "Results appear to indicate…" / "Participants tend to perform better when…"

grammarTable.subject: Adverb hedges
grammarTable.example: "The effect is probably due to…" / "This is likely related to…" / "Apparently, the mechanism differs across groups."

grammarTable.subject: Approximators
grammarTable.verb: approximately / roughly / around / about / up to / as many as / at least
grammarTable.example: "Approximately 60% of participants responded." / "Up to 40% showed improvement."

grammarTable.subject: Limiting expressions
grammarTable.verb: in some cases / under certain conditions / in this context
grammarTable.example: "In some cases, the effect may be reversed." / "Under controlled conditions, results are consistent."

grammarTable.subject: Reporting with caution
grammarTable.example: "It is likely that further studies will confirm this." / "It remains unclear whether the effect is causal."

grammarExtra.title: Modal Verbs for Hedging: Degrees of Certainty

rows.form: will = certainty (avoid in science unless proven)
rows.example: "The drug WILL cure the disease." ❌ (too strong) → "The drug MAY reduce symptoms." ✅

rows.form: should = expectation based on evidence
rows.example: "Based on the data, these results should be replicable."

rows.form: may/might = possibility (might = slightly more uncertain)
rows.example: "This may indicate a novel mechanism." / "The effect might be artefactual."

rows.form: could = theoretical possibility
rows.example: "This could suggest a relationship between the variables."

grammarExtra.title: Hedging Verbs: From Strong to Weak

rows.form: Strong (avoid over-use in science): prove, demonstrate, show
rows.example: "The data demonstrates a correlation." (can be used when evidence is very strong)

rows.form: Medium: suggest, indicate, imply, point to
rows.example: "The findings suggest a link between X and Y." / "Results indicate that further research is needed."

rows.form: Weak / cautious: appear to, seem to, tend to, be consistent with
rows.example: "Participants appear to benefit from the intervention." / "This seems to suggest…"

rows.form: "Tend to" = common pattern, not universal
rows.example: "Older participants tend to show larger effects." (= usually, but not always)

rows.form: approximately / roughly / around / about + number
rows.example: "Approximately 300 participants were enrolled." / "Around 70% showed improvement."

rows.form: up to + number (= maximum)
rows.example: "Up to 40% of participants may experience side effects." (= the maximum observed)

rows.form: as many as + number (= surprising high maximum)
rows.example: "As many as 80% responded positively in the first trial."

rows.form: at least + number (= minimum)
rows.example: "At least 50 replications are needed to establish a reliable estimate."

rows.form: It is possible/likely/probable that + clause
rows.example: "It is likely that the effect will be smaller in a larger sample."

rows.form: It remains/is unclear/uncertain whether/how + clause
rows.example: "It remains unclear whether the effect is causal or merely correlational."

rows.form: It should be noted that / It is worth mentioning that
rows.example: "It should be noted that the sample was not representative of the general population."

rows.form: There is some/little/no evidence that + clause
rows.example: "There is some evidence that meditation reduces cortisol levels."

rows.form: ❌ Under-hedging: "This proves that exercise cures depression."
rows.example: ✅ "These results suggest that exercise may significantly reduce depressive symptoms."

rows.form: ❌ Over-hedging: "It is possible that something might perhaps be the case."
rows.example: ✅ "It is possible that X contributes to Y." (one hedge is usually enough)

rows.form: ❌ Wrong modal: "The drug will help patients."
rows.example: ✅ "The drug may help patients with this condition."

rows.form: ❌ Missing limitation: "Meditation reduces stress." (always true?)
rows.example: ✅ "In this study, meditation appeared to reduce stress in adults aged 30–50."

exercises.instruction: Choose the most appropriate hedging modal.
exercises.text: "The effect ___ be larger in populations with greater genetic diversity."
exercises.hint: "May" = possibility — appropriate for cautious scientific claim

exercises.text: "The data ___ that a correlation exists between the two variables, though causation cannot yet be established."
"___ 65% of participants reported a reduction in symptoms after 8 weeks."

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct impersonal hedging structure.
exercises.text: "It ___ unclear whether the effect is causal or merely correlational at this stage."
exercises.hint: "It remains unclear whether" = formal, impersonal hedge

exercises.instruction: Which is the most appropriately hedged claim?
opts: "Exercise may significantly reduce depressive symptoms in some populations."
"Exercise perhaps could maybe help a bit."
exercises.correct: "Exercise may significantly reduce depressive symptoms in some populations."
exercises.hint: One modal + specific language + limiting expression = well-hedged

exercises.text: "___ 40 independent replications have been conducted — a remarkable level of replication for this field."
"Participants ___ to respond more positively to the treatment when given clear instructions."
exercises.hint: "Tend to" = common pattern but not universal — appropriate hedge

exercises.instruction: Complete with an appropriate impersonal hedge.
exercises.text: "___ likely ___ the sample size will need to be increased for the effect to reach significance."
exercises.hint: "It is likely that + clause" = formal impersonal hedging

exercises.instruction: Which approximator expresses the maximum possible figure?
exercises.text: "___ 80% of participants showed improvement in the first trial." (surprising maximum)
exercises.hint: "As many as + number" = surprisingly high maximum figure

exercises.text: "The drug cures the condition." → The drug ___ treat the condition in most patients under controlled conditions."
exercises.hint: Modal verb ("may") or hedging verb ("appears to") softens the claim

exercises.text: "The effect was consistent ___ controlled laboratory conditions." (restricting the claim)
exercises.hint: "Under + conditions" = limiting the scope of the claim

exercises.text: "There is ___ ___ that the intervention is effective in preventing relapse." (some evidence)
exercises.hint: "There is some evidence that + clause" — cautious positive claim

exercises.instruction: Which modal is most appropriate for a cautious scientific prediction?
exercises.text: "Based on current evidence, this treatment ___ reduce mortality rates by up to 20%."
exercises.hint: "Could" = theoretical possibility — appropriate for prediction without full evidence

exercises.text: "The results ___ ___ be explained by chance alone, given the sample size." (= it is unlikely)
exercises.hint: "Cannot be explained" or "unlikely to be explained" — appropriate hedging negative

exercises.instruction: Which sentence is appropriately hedged for a scientific paper?
opts: "This study proves that open data is better."
"These findings suggest that open data practices may be associated with higher replication rates."
"It is definitely the case that open data helps."
exercises.correct: "These findings suggest that open data practices may be associated with higher replication rates."

opts: Using too few modals and approximators
Using so many hedging words that the claim becomes meaningless
Making claims that are too strong
exercises.correct: Using so many hedging words that the claim becomes meaningless
exercises.hint: "It is possible that something might perhaps be the case" = too many hedges

questions.text: "The results ___ indicate a causal relationship — but further research is needed." (medium-certainty hedge)
questions.hint: "May + verb" = possibility — appropriate cautious scientific claim

questions.text: "The data ___ a strong correlation between the two variables." (hedging reporting verb — not "proves")

questions.hint: "Approximately + number" = standard approximator in scientific writing

questions.text: "It remains ___ whether the observed improvements are due to the drug or to the placebo effect." (uncertain)
questions.hint: "It remains unclear/uncertain whether" = formal impersonal hedge

questions.text: "Participants ___ to perform better when they are given frequent feedback." (common pattern but not universal)
questions.hint: "Tend to" = common pattern, not absolute rule — appropriate hedge

questions.text: "This proves that the drug works" is an appropriately hedged scientific claim.
questions.hint: "Proves" is too strong — use "suggests," "indicates," or "appears to show"

questions.text: "___ 80% of patients responded positively in the first trial." (surprising maximum)
questions.hint: "As many as + number" = surprisingly high maximum figure

questions.text: "___ is possible that some of the effect may be artefactual." (impersonal hedge)
questions.hint: "It is possible that + clause" = standard impersonal hedging

questions.text: "There ___ ___ evidence that pre-registration reduces publication bias." (some but not definitive)
questions.hint: "There is some evidence that" = cautious positive claim

questions.text: "The treatment ___ reduce symptoms in some patients." (theoretical possibility)
"___ 50 independent replications were conducted on this finding." (minimum figure)
Which sentence is the most appropriately hedged for academic writing?
opts: "Open science might perhaps possibly help a little."
"Open science practices appear to be associated with improved replication rates."
"Open science will certainly solve the replication crisis."
questions.correct: "Open science practices appear to be associated with improved replication rates."
questions.hint: "Appear to be associated with" = well-hedged scientific claim
